html:
Nom Ti Pom is one of the local divisions of the Wintu, a Wintuan-speaking people of the upper Sacramento River valley in northern California, just north of today's Redding. The Wintu lived in small villages and held their land in band territories, eating salmon from the rivers and acorns from the oak groves.

From the 1850s the Gold Rush brought miners, massacres and disease that destroyed most Wintu villages. In the 1940s Shasta Dam flooded much of what remained, including villages and burial grounds. See also Northern Wintu and Kl'bal Pom Wintu.
